scope: Isolated candidate only: default WritebackStage=0 and existing CLINT unchanged. Register raw timer interrupt once at SoC integration on ungated clk_i. No shipping RTL, constraints or active layout changes. Single new storage bit is not radiation-qualified. Functional simulation and final mapping/timing remain required.
motivation: Measured ECO7 path from SECDED mtime storage through MTIP and core control to fetch_addr_q exceeds the slow setup budget. Separate the comparator and core combinational cones; leave mtime reads and compare registers untouched.
inference: The ISA permits delayed reflection of the mtime/mtimecmp comparison in MTIP. This supports investigating a bounded one-clock delivery delay, but does not prove system correctness or validate an implementation.
commands: SOC_MEM_RDREG=1 SOC_REQ_REG=1 SOC_RF_SYNPRE=1 SOC_APB_TIMEOUT=256 timeout 1800 stdbuf -oL -eL bash hw/soc/out/external-review-20260919/timer-irq-register-probe/sim_soc.sh hw/soc/out/external-review-20260919/timer-irq-register-probe/sim
limitations: Adds one unprotected state bit; a protected implementation, synthesis cost, timing, fault controls and final physical flow would be required before adoption.
Architectural source permits delayed MTIP updates, but is not a substitute for whole-system validation.
No change to shipping RTL, timing constraints or active route.
